find: In a dental practice, for example, a dental nurse treats patients with toothache, carries out check-ups and provides oral health advice.
replace: In a dental practice, for example, a dental nurse supports dental professionals during treatment and provides oral health advice.
note: F1: Dental nurses do not diagnose disease or plan treatment.

find: A dental nurse applying this value explains two treatment options clearly — including the risks and benefits of each — and invites the patient to decide.
replace: A dentist applying this value explains treatment options clearly — including the risks and benefits of each — and invites the patient to decide.
note: F2: Treatment planning is outside a dental nurse’s general scope.

find: <dfn class="term" data-def="The right of a service user to make their own decisions about their care and daily life.">individuality</dfn>
replace: <dfn class="term" data-def="Recognising each service user as a unique person with their own needs, preferences and life history.">individuality</dfn>
note: F3: The original definition described choice, not individuality.

find: <dfn class="term" data-def="A person-centred value that protects a service user's right to make their own choices without interference.">autonomy</dfn>
replace: <dfn class="term" data-def="A person-centred value that means offering and respecting a service user's choices about their care and daily life.">choice</dfn>
note: F4: Choice is the named R032 value.

find: The non-verbal communication skills listed in the spec are: adapting type/method to needs; eye contact; facial expressions; gestures; positioning (including space, height and personal space); positive body language (no crossed arms/legs); and sense of humour.
replace: The specification lists: adapting type/method to needs; eye contact; facial expressions; gestures; positioning (including space, height and personal space); positive body language (no crossed arms/legs); and sense of humour.
note: F5: The specification does not define this as an eight-item list.

find: Makaton is not a standalone language — it supplements spoken language rather than replacing it.
replace: Makaton is a flexible communication programme that uses signs, symbols and speech.
note: F6: Makaton signs and symbols can be used on their own as well as with speech.

find: Unlike BSL, Makaton is always used alongside speech rather than as a replacement for it.
replace: Unlike BSL, Makaton is a communication programme that can be adapted to an individual’s needs, using signs, symbols and speech.
note: F6: Makaton signs and symbols can be used on their own as well as with speech.

find: Using anti-bacterial sprays on surfaces kills bacteria and viruses on tables, door handles, bed rails and work surfaces.
replace: Using anti-bacterial sprays on surfaces can reduce bacteria on tables, door handles, bed rails and work surfaces. Use a suitable disinfectant, following its label and local policy, where disinfection is required.
note: F7: Not all products kill bacteria and viruses.

find: Disposable gloves protect the hands during any direct contact with a service user’s skin, wounds, bodily fluids or waste. They are also worn once and discarded.
replace: Disposable gloves are worn when exposure to blood, body fluids, non-intact skin or mucous membranes is anticipated. They are single use and discarded after the task.
note: F8: Glove use must be risk-based, not routine for all intact-skin contact.

find: Overshoes are worn over footwear in sterile environments such as operating theatres or clean-room settings to prevent contaminants being carried in from outside.
replace: Overshoes may be used where local policy requires them. They should be discarded after use and are not generally used in health and care settings.
note: F9: Overshoes are not generally used in health and care settings.

find: Surgical garments and scrubs are the standardised clothing worn by surgical teams: they are made from smooth, easy-to-clean material, have no pockets where pathogens could collect, and are laundered at high temperatures. Scrubs are also used by nurses, healthcare assistants and allied health professionals in clinical settings as a hygienic alternative to street clothing.
replace: Surgical garments and scrubs are clinical workwear used by surgical teams. They are used and laundered in line with local policy.
note: F10: Scrubs can have pockets; use and laundering are set locally.

find: A hospital ward will additionally require clinical waste disposal protocols, surgical scrubs for ward staff, and strict PPE protocols for barrier nursing of infectious patients.
replace: A hospital ward will additionally use clinical-waste procedures and PPE based on the task and infection risk.
note: F11: Surgical scrubs are not a universal ward requirement.

find: A residential home for adults with dementia will have electronic swipe card systems on all main doors (to prevent residents leaving unsupervised), window locks throughout, key monitoring, and all external visitors signed in and issued with badges.
replace: A residential home for adults with dementia may use access controls, key monitoring and visitor sign-in. Any restriction on a resident must be individually assessed and proportionate to the risk.
note: F12: Restrictions must be individually assessed and proportionate.
